slides.title: Rvalue Reference Syntax and Rules
slides.prompt: Introduced in C++11, rvalue references (declared with &&) bind exclusively to rvalues. They enable functions to detect temporaries and transfer resources instead of copying.

slides.title: Rvalue Reference Declaration
slides.prompt: Fill in the token used to declare an rvalue reference parameter type for std::string.

slides.title: Named Rvalue Reference Variable Category
slides.prompt: Given 'int&& r = 42;', what is the value category of the named variable 'r' itself when evaluated in an expression?
options: Lvalue (because 'r' has a name and address)
Rvalue (because its type is an rvalue reference)
slides.correctAnswer: Lvalue (because 'r' has a name and address)

slides.title: Binding Non-Const Lvalue References
slides.prompt: Fill in the correct keyword to complete the valid binding rule: Non-const lvalue references bind only to ___values.
slides.codeSnippet:
int x = 100;
int& lref = x; // Valid because 'x' is an ___value

slides.title: Overload Resolution: Lvalue vs Rvalue Ref
slides.prompt: If void print(const std::string&) and void print(std::string&&) are both defined, which overload is selected for print(std::string("data"))?
options: void print(std::string&&) because rvalue reference matches temporaries exactly
void print(const std::string&) because const references take priority
Selected randomly depending on compiler settings
slides.correctAnswer: void print(std::string&&) because rvalue reference matches temporaries exactly

slides.title: Casting Lvalue to Rvalue Reference
slides.prompt: Fill in the static_cast type expression equivalent to std::move(x) for integer x.

slides.title: Modifying Data via Rvalue Reference
slides.prompt: Can you mutate the underlying state of an object bound through a non-const rvalue reference T&&?
options: Yes, rvalue references provide mutable access to the temporary resource
No, all rvalue references are automatically read-only
Only if the type T is a primitive integer
slides.correctAnswer: Yes, rvalue references provide mutable access to the temporary resource

slides.title: Rvalue Reference Lifetime Rule
slides.prompt: Fill in the missing word: An rvalue reference variable extends the lifetime of a temporary object to which it is ___.
slides.codeSnippet: std::string&& ref = getTemporaryString(); // Temporary object is ___ to ref

slides.title: Const Rvalue Reference Usage
slides.prompt: Why are const rvalue references (const T&&) rarely used in C++ codebases?
options: They prevent resource stealing/moving while providing no benefits over const T&
They are illegal syntax that triggers compiler errors
They force implicit deep copies on every function call
They can only bind to static variable addresses
slides.correctAnswer: They prevent resource stealing/moving while providing no benefits over const T&

slides.prompt: Fill in the return type symbol for a method designed to return an internal member as an expiring rvalue reference.
